record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: What is the exact computational complexity class of the two-dimensional PEPS zero-testing problem?

evidence.quote: Question 14 Which is the exact complexity class for 2D PEPS zero-testing?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a two-dimensional lattice is specified by placing, at each site v of an n × n square lattice, a tensor A^{(v)} with one physical index of dimension d and four virtual indices of dimension at most D (one for each lattice direction), and contracting all matching virtual indices between nearest-neighbor sites. The contraction yields a vector |ψ⟩ in the Hilbert space (ℂ^d)^{⊗ n²}.

The 2D PEPS zero-testing problem is the following decision problem:

  Input: a description of a PEPS on an n × n square lattice, given by the list of local tensors {A^{(v)}} (with rational or finite-precision complex entries) together with the bond dimension D and physical dimension d.
  Question: is the resulting global state |ψ⟩ equal to the zero vector?

Determine the exact computational complexity class of this decision problem. That is, identify a complexity class C such that 2D PEPS zero-testing is C-complete under polynomial-time (many-one) reductions, with matching upper and lower bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: Known results show 2D PEPS zero-testing is NP-hard, and there exist families of PEPS for which zero-testing is undecidable, but no tight characterization (matching upper and lower bounds in a single complexity class) for the general 2D PEPS zero-testing problem appears in the literature. The exact complexity class therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of PEPS zero testing
status_evidence.snippet: Zero-testing for tensor network states is NP-hard, and there are PEPS families for which it is undecidable.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds (NP-hardness, undecidability for special families) are known but no matching tight class for general 2D PEPS zero-testing.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate complexity of PEPS-related decision problems, indicating the exact class for general PEPS zero-testing is not yet pinned down.
status_evidence.claim: The question of the exact complexity class for 2D PEPS zero-testing is still being studied.
